headline: French Farmers Turn Climate Change Into Opportunity With Homegrown Tropical Fruit
meta_description: South of France growers are cultivating bananas, papayas, and mangoes in greenhouses, transforming warming temperatures into a chance for local, pesticide-free…
summary_short: As southern France warms, innovative farmers are growing tropical fruits like bananas and papayas locally—eliminating long-distance shipping while maintaining French qua…
body:
Facing rising temperatures and unpredictable heatwaves, farmers across southern France are reimagining their fields with an unexpected solution: tropical fruit. Dominique Berdin, likely France's only papaya grower, cultivates about 20 varieties of tropical produce—including passion fruit and pineapples—pesticide-free inside her Var Department greenhouse year-round. Nearby, agronomist Johan Bultel experiments with 26 different banana varieties sourced from places as distant as Honduras and the Reunion Islands, betting that at least one will thrive even through French winters. These aren't isolated experiments but part of a broader shift among local growers recognizing that warming temperatures, once a threat, now offer genuine economic opportunity. "If we are willing to adapt it might turn into an opportunity to grow our own tropical fruit instead of shipping it from across the globe," Berdin told France24.

The movement reflects real desperation turned to pragmatism. Isabelle Pertois abandoned her organic vegetable operation after scorching summers became routine, inspired instead by farming practices in Spain and North Africa. She now grows tomatoes and squash beneath citrus tree shade, with banana trees already pushing through her greenhouse roof. Another local dragon fruit grower has doubled yields by adopting these new cropping strategies. What makes this shift remarkable isn't just innovation under pressure—it's the collective nature of the effort. Pertois, Berdin, Bultel, and numerous unnamed neighbors are learning and adapting together, demonstrating that agricultural resilience doesn't require sacrificing the excellence French produce represents.

These farmers embody a quiet defiance: climate change arrives, but so does opportunity. By growing tropical fruit locally, they reduce shipping emissions while building a new agricultural identity rooted in their transformed landscape.

Johan Bultel cultivates 26 banana varieties from Honduras and Reunion Islands
Isabelle Pertois shifted from organic vegetables to tropical fruit farming
